channel.title: Orbi Blog
channel.description: Notes from shipping Orbi in the open: delivery runs, failures, fixes, and measurements.

item.title: GitSpawn and the agent that never asks
item.description: A git flaw hit seven coding agents by skipping their approval prompts. Orbi has none to skip, so we shipped a fix, checked who really runs git, and reverted it.

item.title: DeepSeek coding agent cost per merged PR
item.description: See how Orbi uses DeepSeek as an unattended coding agent, what each merged PR costs, why cache reads matter, and how to connect your own API key in practice.

item.title: Why Orbi is open source again
item.description: Orbi began on Apache-2.0 and switched to the Sustainable Use License on Sep 4. From v0.5.44 it is AGPL-3.0, or the SUL if AGPL is ruled out. Here is why.

item.title: The k8e etcd ticket that closed too early
item.description: Orbi wrote an etcd test suite for k8e, a 497-star Kubernetes distro. It was rejected, fixed and merged, and the four-phase issue closed after phase one.

item.title: How one slash command got its shape
item.description: A close look at the name, syntax, regex anchor, and registry behind one in-ticket command, compared with Prow and bors-ng and checked against their source.

item.title: The engine waited for an answer users could not give
item.description: Our engine paused for a human decision, then asked tenants to use a command they did not have. We found three versions of the same mistake in one afternoon.

item.title: Seven steps of an Orbi Cloud setup, on video
item.description: An 83-second video follows the Orbi Cloud setup from GitHub sign-in to a tagged release and subscription. The final step starts paid Cloud delivery here.

item.title: What an autonomous coding agent does when it says no
item.description: Most autonomous coding agents stop at a pull request. Here, a second model rejected the diff twice, while the commits and release remain available to inspect.

item.title: Claude Code in Actions: who presses merge?
item.description: Claude Code Action can implement and review pull requests in your runner. It stops before merge and release. Here is the evidence-backed layer for both.

item.title: The Docker image made it out on try three
item.description: The orbi image reached GHCR and Docker Hub on its third run. The first two failures involved build context and Dockerfile paths; the last was an invalid tag.
